newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran forces fire missiles in Gulf war games.
newsitem.headline: Iran forces fire missiles in Gulf war games.

text.p: Iran said it had successfully fired missiles, tested long-range rocket launchers and staged electronic warfare exercises in the Gulf on Friday.
State-run Tehran radio said Iranian forces carrying out a major 10-day manoeuvre scored "precise hits" with an air-to-sea missile named Piroozi-75 (Victory-75).
It quoted an unnamed military official as saying a locally designed and built missile launcher named Fajr (Dawn) was also successfully tested.
Electronic attack and defence operations, monitoring of enemy units, jamming radar and diverting enemy rockets were among the exercises carried out, the radio said.

Some 100 ships, including destroyers, gunboats, hovercraft and Iran's two Russian-built submarines, backed by 40 planes and helicopters were taking part in the exercises in the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman which were due to end on Saturday.

Iranian media earlier said the Piroozi-75 missile had a range of 90 miles (145 km). They said it was an updated version of the Silkworm missile, suggesting Iranian technicians had improved the Chinese-made missile.
Iran's navy commander last week condemned the Western military presence in the Gulf as "a kind of occupation" but said Iran's exercise "does not challenge anyone and does not signal any tension".
